title: Travis Kelce Celebrates 100th Game at Arrowhead Stadium With Taylor Swift-Coded Comment: ‘It’s Pretty Awesome’
summary: The Chiefs tight end paid tribute to his professional home of 14 years while also shouting out Swift's Eras Tour show at his home stadium.
contentText:
Travis Kelce has plenty of great memories playing at the Kansas City Chiefs’ home stadium. In fact, on Sunday (Nov. 22), three-time Super Bowl champ Kelce marked a new career milestone in his 14-year journey with the team when he became just the fourth player in franchise history to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead.

He discussed that major stat on this week’s episode of his New Heights podcast with brother Jason Kelce, including passing former Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski in total career touchdowns (110-to-108) and why his good memories also, of course, include ones tied to his wife Taylor Swift .

“One hundred games, dude, it feels pretty awesome right now,” Travis said of his home game high point. “To think about that legacy of that stadium, man and it’s pretty crazy to think they’re moving on from that stadium, because of all the history that’s happened over the years and history of the franchise and everything.” The Chiefs have announced plans to leave Arrowhead when their lease expires after the 2030 NFL season.

Then Travis dug into what it’s been like playing at Arrowhead all those years, adding a subtle nod to Swift, whose Eras Tour touched down at the stadium on July 7 and 8, 2023; Kelce was in attendance on night two.

“You know it’s been home for me for 14 years, and it’s been one of my favorite places to go to play and to watch not only football, but musical events and I’ve had so much history and so many things that mean so much to me happen at Arrowhead that a hundred games, it’s pretty awesome to hit that milestone,” Kelce said in a subtle nod to Swift’s history playing at the 55,000-seat venue.

Jason, however, questioned Travis’ “cheers to 100 more” pledge after the game, reminding his 37-year-old brother that “you’re not gonna play a f–kin’ 100 more games. What are you talkin’ about?” Travis, who has not yet said whether this is his last season with the Chiefs, fully admitted, “yeah, you’re right, I won’t. But … cheers to 100 more. Who knows how many I’ll get to?”

Asked if that comment was proof he’s coming back for one more season next year, Travis let out a big sigh and said he was not confirming anything. He is, however, psyched for Thursday’s (Nov. 24) Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Buffalo Bills, who, at 9-1, have the best record in the league. “Gotta keep this thing f–king rolling into the old Turkey bowl baby, let’s go!”

Kelce has spent his entire career with the Chiefs and eight months before he won his third championship with the team in February 2024, he saw Swift at Arrowhead in July 2023, where he famously missed out on his chance to get her a friendship bracele t with his number on it. Swift made the scene at her first Chiefs home game in September 2023 and the pair got married at New York’s Madison Square Garden in July of this year.
